newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Thousands of Zaireans flee their country-UNHCR.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Zaireans flee their country-UNHCR.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR said on Tuesday that thousands of Zaireans, among them officers and businessmen, have been arriving in the nearby Central African Republic since the overthrow of president Mobutu Sese Seko.

About 2,000 Zairean refugees have converged in Mobayu region across the Ubangi river border from Mobutu's former jungle palace Gbadolite in the north of the vast African republic, UNHCR spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole told a news briefing in Geneva.
The arrival of thousands more had been reported from other locations along the river straddling the frontier with the Central African Republic, she said.

The exodus began after Mobutu fled Kinshasa for Gbadolite and Laurent Kabila's rebels entered the capital at the weekend. Mobutu later left Gbadolite for the west African state of Togo where he is resting, security sources said.

Most of those crossing to the Central African Republic were women and children but there were also substantial numbers of men, members of the Zairean business community and former military officers, O'Toole said.
Zaireans were also crossing into neighbouring Congo, she said without giving figures.
Reports at the weekend said about 30 members of Mobutu's immediate family fled to Congo on Saturday to await a flight into exile in Morocco after the rebels moved into Kinshasa.
Mobutu's soldier son, Kongolo, and the commander of the feared presidential guard, General Nzimbi Ngbale, were said to be among those waiting in Congo.
